rules.title: Writ entry keys
rules.statement: writ_entry ::= (STRING | '-' INTEGER | INTEGER) ':' writ_val ; a map key is a quoted string, a negative integer, or a non-negative integer. A '-' INTEGER key carries LO_NEG.
rules.divergence: No Rust analogue; Writ data-literal grammar.

rules.title: Writ CFG type-slot
rules.statement: writ_val may be '<' 'type' ':' IDENT path_step+ '>' producing a CFG_SLOT_TYPE (slot extraction keeping an IDENT-only head followed by path steps).
rules.divergence: No Rust analogue; Writ embedded-type slot.

rules.title: Writ runtime capture placeholders
rules.statement: Inside a Writ literal, '${' expr '}' captures an arbitrary expression (WRIT_CAP_EXPR) and '$' IDENT captures a named binding (WRIT_CAP_IDENT) as a runtime value.

rules.title: Optional @ on nested Writ aggregates
rules.statement: A nested writ_map / writ_array inside a writ_val may optionally be prefixed by '@'; '@'-prefixed and bare forms are equivalent.
rules.divergence: No Rust analogue; Writ literal nesting.

rules.title: Writ scalar values
rules.statement: writ_val scalars: RAW_STRING/STRING -> WRIT_STR; FLOAT -> WRIT_FLOAT; '-' INTEGER -> WRIT_NEG_INT; INTEGER -> WRIT_INT; 'true'/'false' -> WRIT_BOOL; 'null' -> WRIT_NULL.
rules.divergence: No Rust analogue; Writ scalar literals.

rules.title: Array literal
rules.statement: arr_lit ::= '[' (expr (',' expr)* ','?)? ']' ; a bracket-delimited comma-separated list of expressions with optional trailing comma.

rules.title: Tuple literal arity
rules.statement: tuple_lit ::= '(' expr ',' expr (',' expr)* ')' | '(' expr ',' ')' ; a tuple literal requires either a single element with a trailing comma, or two or more comma-separated elements. '(expr)' alone is not a tuple.

rules.title: Closure parameter type may be omitted
rules.statement: closure_param allows the type annotation to be omitted: '|x|' is accepted as well as '|x: T|'. Forms: '&mut IDENT', '&IDENT', 'ref IDENT: T', 'mut IDENT: T', 'mut IDENT', '(pat_binding_list): T', 'IDENT: T', 'IDENT'. The omitted type is inferred from the surrounding fn(T)->R formal at the call site.

rules.title: Closure expression forms
rules.statement: closure_expr is '|' closure_param_list? '|' or '||' (OR token), optionally preceded by 'move' and optionally followed by '-> type', with a body that is either a block or (tried after block forms) a single expression. '|x| expr' / '|| expr' are brace-less expression-body closures; the body expr stops at the enclosing ',' / ')'.

rules.title: quote_item! macro
rules.statement: quote_item_expr ::= 'quote_item' '!' '{' item* '}' ; body is zero or more item declarations producing a typed AST (item-blob) literal.
rules.divergence: No Rust analogue (Rust uses macro_rules!/proc-macro quote).

rules.title: quote_expr! macro
rules.statement: quote_expr_expr ::= 'quote_expr' '!' '{' expr '}' ; body is a single expression producing a typed AST (expr-blob) literal.

rules.title: quote_ty! macro
rules.statement: quote_ty_expr ::= 'quote_ty' '!' '{' type_ref '}' ; body is a single type expression producing a first-class Type literal (same Type{kind,name,size} shape as type_of::<T>()).

rules.title: Parenthesised expression
rules.statement: paren_expr ::= '(' expr ')' ; a single parenthesised expression (not a tuple).

rules.title: Type parameter list
rules.statement: type_param_list ::= '<' type_param (',' type_param)* ','? '>' ; also reused for specialisation patterns (<i32>, <*T>, <[T;4]>). Distinguishing type-var vs concrete is deferred to sema, not grammar.

rules.title: HRTB for<...> binder parsed then dropped
rules.statement: hrtb_binder ::= 'for' '<' LIFETIME (',' LIFETIME)* ','? '>' may prefix any trait_bound. Lifetimes are not tracked structurally, so for<'a> Trait<...> is semantically equivalent to Trait<...> (binder parsed into a disposable head).
rules.divergence: Lifetimes not structurally tracked: HRTB binder is accepted but discarded (Rust enforces it).

rules.title: Relaxed bound ?Trait
rules.statement: trait_bound may be '?' IDENT (RELAXED). Grammatically any '?Ident' is accepted; sema rejects anything other than '?Sized' (which opts a type parameter out of the implicit Sized bound).

rules.title: Trait bound forms
rules.statement: A trait_bound is an IDENT optionally with generic args 'Name<bound_arg_list>' or Fn-family parenthesized form 'Name(closure_type_args?) ('-> type)?', each optionally HRTB-prefixed.

rules.title: Associated-type equality in bound args
rules.statement: bound_arg_list mixes positional type/lifetime args and associated-type equality clauses; bound_arg ::= IDENT '=' type_ref (ASSOC_EQ_BIND) | type_or_lt_arg.

rules.title: Lifetime parameter with outlives bound
rules.statement: lifetime_param ::= LIFETIME (':' LIFETIME ('+' LIFETIME)*)? ; a lifetime parameter optionally carries one or more outlives bounds.

rules.title: Type parameter forms
rules.statement: type_param admits: lifetime_param; 'IDENT: lifetime_param (+ lifetime_param)*' (type-outlives); ptr/arr specialisation patterns; const params 'const IDENT: T', 'const IDENT...: T' (variadic), 'const #IDENT: T'; variadic type param 'IDENT... (: bounds)?'; metavar '#IDENT (: bounds)?'; 'IDENT: bounds (= default)?'; 'IDENT = default'; or bare 'IDENT'. A repeat-group '#(type_param), *' expands variadically.
rules.divergence: Logos additions: variadic type/const params ('...'), metavar params ('#'), repeat-group expansion (no Rust equivalent).

rules.title: Type parameter default
rules.statement: A type parameter may carry a default via 'IDENT (: bounds)? = type_ref'; the default type applies when the argument is omitted at instantiation.

rules.title: Type argument list
rules.statement: type_arg_list ::= type_or_lt_arg (',' type_or_lt_arg)* ','? ; generic instantiation argument list (e.g. Vec<i32>).

rules.title: Call argument list
rules.statement: call_arg_list ::= expr (',' expr)* ','? ; a call site's value-argument list with optional trailing comma.

rules.title: Package-qualified free-function call
rules.statement: A call 'IDENT path_dot_ident+ '::' IDENT ('::' '<' type_arg_list '>')? '(' call_arg_list? ')'' resolves a free fn by its dotted package path (RECEIVER = first segment, QUAL_PARTS = rest); this disambiguates same-named free fns across packages (e.g. logos.lang.mem::replace vs logos.lang.ptr::replace).
rules.divergence: Logos path model: '.'-separated package path + '::'-item (vs Rust all-'::').

rules.title: Turbofish on the type
rules.statement: 'Type::<T>::method(args)' is a STATIC_CALL applying type args <T> to the type before selecting an associated fn/method/new; 'Type::<T>(args)' / 'new::<T>(args)' / 'null::<T>(args)' are GENERIC_CALL with the type args on the callee.

rules.title: UFCS qualified-path call
rules.statement: '<Type as Trait>::method(args)' dispatches on the concrete Type; the trait qualifier is consumed and dropped because the type-dispatch already resolves the method.
rules.divergence: Trait qualifier in <T as Tr>::m is dropped (Rust uses it for disambiguation).

rules.title: Turbofish on the method
rules.statement: 'Type::method::<T>(args)' applies type args <T> to the associated method's own generics (distinct from Type::<T>::method); must be matched before plain 'Type::method(args)'.

rules.title: Static / associated call
rules.statement: 'Type::IDENT(args)' and 'Type::new(args)' are STATIC_CALLs invoking an associated function (including the 'new' constructor) of the receiver type.

rules.title: Metavariable call
rules.statement: '#IDENT(args)' and '#(expr)(args)' invoke a callee named by a metavariable (NAME_VAR) or by an evaluated expression, used in metaprogramming-expanded call sites.
rules.divergence: No Rust analogue; metaprogramming callee splice.

rules.title: Free function call
rules.statement: 'IDENT(args)', 'new(args)', and 'null(args)' are plain free-function CALLs by name.

rules.title: Writ map literal
rules.statement: writ_map ::= '{' (writ_entry (',' writ_entry)* ','?)? '}' ; a brace-delimited, comma-separated list of key:value entries (writ_entry), producing {CODE:MAP, ITEMS:[...]}. The entry list may be empty and a single trailing comma after the last entry is permitted.

rules.title: Writ embedded type literal `<type: T>`
rules.statement: A Writ value may embed a Logos Type as a first-class value via `'<' 'type' ':' simple_type '>'`, producing a WRIT_TYPE_LIT node carrying the rendered type T. Any simple_type is accepted, including generic instantiations (e.g. Vec<u8>, Result<T,E>); it renders back as `<type: T>`.
